drop: Genesis 9:5 (keep 9:6 only; 9:5-6 stays whole under the secondary 'The blood of man')
concepts.why: Passage length (all readers): Genesis 9:5 is about accounting for a life shed, longer than the concept needs; 9:6 carries 'in His own image'. All notes checked and are exact quotations. Name is the texts' own phrase (Gen 1:27, 9:6); Gen 5:1 and James 3:9 say 'likeness' rather than 'image', which is acceptable as the theme's own pair.

note_fixes: Mark 10:6-8: the note ('So they are no longer two, but one flesh') is exact but is not the concept; use 'God made them male and female' and shorten the passage to Mark 10:6, leaving 'one flesh' to the secondary 'Male and female -> one flesh' (Gen 2:24; Mark 10:8)
concepts.why: Name against passages: Genesis 2:18 and 2:22-24 do not say 'male and female He created them' (they tell of the woman's making from the man and of one flesh); they are already carried by the secondary 'Male and female -> one flesh', so they duplicate it. Reformed/Baptist (complementarian) and Wesleyan/Pentecostal (egalitarian) readers would each hear Genesis 2:18 ('helper') and the rib account placed under the image as a ruling on whether the image is shared equally or ordered; the Genesis 1:27, 5:2 and Matthew 19:4 core is the texts' own phrase and takes no side.

Academic scholar / all readers: James 3:7 is an aside in a passage about the tongue; it says animals are tamed by man, not that rule was given to man, so it shares the idea in passing and does not hold the concept. Hebrews 2:8 stays because it quotes Psalm 8's 'placed everything under his feet' and says 'at present we do not see everything subject to him', in its own words. All notes checked and exact.

Name against passages: Genesis 2:17 forbids the tree and says nothing of being like God; the tree is already named in Genesis 3:5 and 3:22. Isaiah 14:14 and Ezekiel 28:2 are kept because each uses the same 'like'/'god' words (Ezekiel 28:2 says 'you are a man and not a god'); the concept does not say these passages are the same story, and none of the nine readers is made to take a side.

concepts.name: To whom will you liken God?
concepts.why: Name against passages: 'You saw no form of any kind' (Deuteronomy 4:15) is what only Deuteronomy 4:12 and 4:15-16 say; Exodus 20:4, Isaiah 40:18, 46:5, Acts 17:29 and Romans 1:23 are about making or comparing a likeness, not about seeing. Isaiah 40:18's question (the front page's own row) names all seven passages; Deuteronomy 4 stays as the reason given. Secular/Jewish reader: 'To whom will you liken God?' is the text's question and fits Deuteronomy 4:15-16 and Exodus 20:4 without any gloss. All notes checked and exact.

Name against passages: only Ephesians 4:22-24, Colossians 3:9-10 and Romans 6:6 speak of an old self and a new self. Romans 12:2 does not mention a self, and 2 Corinthians 4:16 speaks of an outer and an inner self, a different pair; both share only 'renewed'. Reformed/Wesleyan readers differ on how far the old self is already dead and how far it is being put off; keeping Romans 6:6 beside Ephesians 4 and Colossians 3 sets the texts' own words side by side and takes no side. 2 Corinthians 4:16 could be offered as a secondary ('Our inner self is being renewed day by day') if wanted.

secondary_or_links: A kingdom of priests -> they will reign: rename to 'A kingdom of priests' and drop Revelation 5:10. Baptist (dispensational) and Catholic/Orthodox readers, and the order of the last things: 'they will reign upon the earth' brings in when and where the reign is, and the arrow from Exodus 19:6 through 1 Peter 2:9 to Revelation sets Israel's calling beside the church's, which the site does not rule on. Exodus 19:6, 1 Peter 2:9 and Revelation 1:6 each say 'kingdom' and 'priests' in so many words and need no arrow.
Moses' face -> the veil over his face: Exodus 34:29-35 is seven verses, longer than the concept needs. Cut to Exodus 34:29 and 34:33-35 (the radiant face and the veil); 2 Corinthians 3:13-16 stays.
Male and female -> one flesh: duplicates concept 2 once Genesis 2:18 and 2:22-24 are dropped there; keep it as the home of Genesis 2:24 and Mark 10:8, as the plain label it is.

Offspring of God -> not like gold or silver or stone (Acts 17:28-29): duplicates concept 7's Acts 17:29. Acceptable as a link, but verse 29 is quoted twice on the same page; keep Acts 17:28 here and leave 17:29 to concept 7 if a trim is wanted.
Links to other themes: no change. 'Messiah/Christology' is a plain label and the nine labels name no side.

missing.sub_theme: Those who make them become like them
missing.why: The texts say that people grow like what they worship ('Those who make them become like them'); this is the counterpart of concepts 7 and 10 (an image made by man against becoming like the God whose image one bears) and is plainly developed under likeness.

missing.sub_theme: The LORD is the Maker of them all
missing.why: The same maker of rich and poor, master and servant, Israelite and stranger: the texts' own ground for how people are to be treated, the neighbour to Genesis 9:6 and James 3:9, and the secondary Acts 17:26 only touches it. Proverbs 14:31 and 17:5 (contempt for the Maker) could be added.

missing.sub_theme: He remembers that we are dust
missing.why: Beside the question of concept 4 and the Genesis 2:7 formation of concept 6, the texts set the being made 'a little lower than the angels' against 'dust' and 'breath'; without it the theme shows only the glory side of what Psalm 8 and Psalm 144 hold together.
